key_insight: Careful circuit-level optimization can measurably suppress logical errors in a surface-code memory on today’s superconducting hardware, even though performance still depends strongly on device placement and noise behavior.
engineering_relevance: This shows that quantum error correction performance on cloud-accessible processors can be improved through QPU and QEC codesign, not just by increasing code distance.
method: Tested rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor across different qubit placements.
Optimized syndrome extraction using short readout, fused measurement/reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout.
Compared logical error rates under standard versus optimized circuits in X and Z memory experiments up to 150 rounds.
evidence_signal: The optimized circuit reduced the median per-round logical error rate by 3.8× in X basis and 1.4× in Z basis, and increasing distance from 3 to 6 lowered per-round error rates from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory.
watch_item: Long-memory runs showed weakening distance advantage and persistent correlations, suggesting nontrivial error sources that may limit scaling on current hardware.
paper_title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
